page: Amazon Web Services r6a.metal is a dedicated bare-metal server designed for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. The system is built on the x86_64 architecture and is powered by AMD EPYC 7R13 processors operating at speeds up to 3.6 GHz. It offers 96 physical cores and 192 dedicated virtual CPUs with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The memory subsystem consists of 1536 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Direct bare-metal access eliminates hypervisor virtualization penalties, granting direct access to processor telemetry, hardware virtualization instructions (AMD SVM), and hardware cryptographic extensions like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark testing reveals substantial computing and memory throughput across intensive workloads. In multithreaded synthetic testing, the system achieves top-tier results, highlighted by a stress-ng multi-core score of 289,144.77 and a PassMark CPU score of 118,709.94. In-memory data structures perform exceptionally well, logging 183.62 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations alongside cached memory read bandwidth exceeding 12,200 GB/sec. Large uncached memory block operations maintain strong transfer rates of 271.4 GB/sec for reads and 129.0 GB/sec for writes. The platform also demonstrates high throughput for software development tasks, registering top-tier results in Clang compilation and ray-tracing tests.

A key architectural consideration is the complete absence of integrated local storage. Because the instance contains no local NVMe or solid-state disks, all persistent and scratch storage must be supplied via network-attached storage volumes. This external dependency is supported by a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, which accommodates high-throughput remote storage access and distributed cluster traffic. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high hardware density of 1.5 TB of RAM and 192 compute threads allows organizations to consolidate multiple smaller instances into a single footprint, lowering per-core operational overhead and software licensing tiers where bare-metal licensing models apply.

The r6a.metal instance is suited for environments requiring massive memory capacity and substantial multithreaded compute without hypervisor overhead. Typical use cases include large-scale in-memory databases such as Redis and Memcached, SAP HANA, high-transaction relational databases, electronic design automation (EDA), distributed memory caching clusters, and large data-transformation pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r6a.metal is a bare-metal memory-optimized server configuration powered by dual AMD EPYC 7R13 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 96 physical cores, 192 dedicated execution threads at clock speeds up to 3.6 GHz, and 1536 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz. The platform features an 8 GB memory-to-vCPU allocation, providing immense RAM capacity without virtualization overhead. The server includes no bundled local NVMe storage, requiring network storage architectures, but provides 50 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth to mitigate external input and output latency. Hardware benchmarks reflect top-tier multithreaded compute throughput and exceptional in-memory operations, highlighted by over 183 million Redis SET operations per second and robust compiler performance. With high resource density on a single bare-metal node, it provides strong qualitative cost efficiency for organizations consolidating sprawling memory footprints. This bare-metal instance is optimal for enterprise in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, electronic design automation, and massive analytics workloads.
